reviews.title: YOU NEED THIS APP + Feedback/Request for developers
reviews.contents: I’ve been using this app since my first baby in 2019 and my one month old. This app is great and definitely what everyone should use if they have a baby themselves. It’s super simple to use and I love the compatibility with the Apple Watch. Makes it super easy especially when you barely have hands when you’re a mom. I’ve been tracking since the day she was born. I’m not extremely religious about it and miss logs here and there but have a majority of good information that gives me insight which is probably what a lot of parents need. Why is my baby fussy? Maybe didn’t get a good nap in that day? I like to look back at the history on when baby had a great day and try to replicate what I did to give baby the best day possible. Obviously with baby, every day is different but if you know what to look out for its much easier as a parent. WHAT I WOULD LOVE TO SEE IN AN UPDATE!! Pretty please 😬😬😬 Hopefully the developers or someone from this app sees this but something if you could adjust the 24 hour time period to your preference. Similar to the “filter” feature.. You could adjust 24 hour cycle - example) from 9pm to 9pm. Something that’s important to me as a mom is sleep and I don’t start bedtime at midnight. I start bedtime at 7 or 8. It would be good to have the visibility of the 24 hour period in which she starts her sleep cycle. Let me know if this makes sense.

reviews.title: Long term user review
reviews.contents:
I’ve used this app every day for a little less than a year now and feel it deserves a review at long last. It was sooooo incredibly helpful when my baby was a newborn. I can thank this app for helping me feel confident to continue my breastfeeding journey and that I have been doing everything right. I love the little updates it gives you about your baby along the way. It’s super user-friendly. Love that if I had any questions from our ped, I didn’t even have to think “what’s feeding been like over the past week/month/3 months?” I know the exact answer every time. 

2 things to mention (for the developers sake). It’s not bad enough to not download the app. I absolutely despise the “wishlist” part of the app. It’s so annoying and if you accidentally click on the tab you have to clear a pop-up every time. Just keep it on your pregnancy app. I don’t need a wishlist after my baby is born. Second frustrating thing is with the solids tracker. If I log a solid, it also changes the “last fed” time on breastfeeding timer as well and we all know that for the first year, solids do not replace breast milk/formula. Just keep them separated bc they show separated in the app. Idk why the timers sync up. I was using the solids part to track new foods but I had to do math to figure out when I ACTUALLY last fed my baby. Too annoying. Might become useful after my baby turns 1.

reviews.title: Strongly recommend for parents
reviews.contents: I love this app an have family who watch my baby also using it. It’s a great app if you can’t remember when you did certain things or just have a very busy life. Keeping track of changings an feeding times have been a huge help in our lives. It’s greatly helped us keep track of how much he’s sleeping as well an the patterns that come with it. When your at the doctors office an they’re always asking you questions regarding how there doing and what schedule they have. This app gives me the ability to answer those questions with confidence and proof. This app graphs all your information accordingly so it’s easy to see how your baby is doing at all times. If you use an app I’d strongly recommend this one. It’s helped us alot an as a first time mom. It’s allowed me to see patterns I didn’t know were there. An has also shown me that there’s alot of little information I didn’t know I wanted. Example being its shown how much all together they consume. It’s gives you times to expect when there going to want food or a nap. On top of it this app shows an tracks bathroom habits as well as monitor activity levels with your child. On top of how great it’s helped they compare all your information with other baby’s to show where your baby should be at goal wise.

reviews.title: Probably the simplest to use but missing some features
reviews.contents:
Good app that has the basics of tracking baby data that syncs over multiple user accounts which is handy if you have your hands full. The biggest issue it has for me is the inability to export raw data. Data availability for the life of the entrants I would say is a big deal if your are a data person and taking the time to record it all. The app allows exports but is limited to 7 days. It is delivered as a vertical chart pdf that you could use to convert to long term charts but would have to remember to keep downloading. Would like to see a longer export range for data and multiple formats of delivery. Or just the ability to change the view of the chart. 

Would like to limit who you are compared with as your baby should be compared against others in its classification (age, sex, etc). A newborn shouldn’t be compared to a 3 yo. Plus, I have seen numbers for comparison to the community that show not many are using the feature as an average wet diaper of 0 either means a lack of use or there are some serious issues with dehydration in the user base. 

Also, the community feature is forced at every turn and it is easy to accidentally post if all you want is to track milestones but end up in one of the community blogs. Because of the ease of tracking, I would say it is worth the download but because they want you to go premium for trends it just is hard to justify the premium feature if they don’t allow lifetime access to the data.

reviews.title: All in all a great app
reviews.contents: I’ve been using this app for about 4 months now and I love it. I do however can not stand the fact that you have to pay a subscription to compare your babies feedings, growth, nap times, and really anything to glow babies, and this is why- Parenting is already so difficult especially if you have multiples or more than one child you’re caring for, we’re constantly stressed about if they got enough to eat or if they’re still hungry or if they’re teething early, or running a fever-we shouldn’t be worried if they’re up to par for their age, so I think we should be able to compare for free. What more could a parent ask for to literally have it all in one app? I also love the community part of this app. It’s nice to know you can talk about more than just babies sometimes and the community in this app and people you follow are so friendly. There aren’t just moms on this app too so I love the fact that it gets dads involved. I love how you can enter notes on loggings, I usually put “gas drops” in them or “ate 28oz in total” for his last feeding just so I can compare for myself to make sure he’s getting enough formula. For parents of babies who struggle to gain or keep weight, this is an important feature that’s just not available for parents who can’t afford to pay for an app. But all in all it’s a great app(from the free side). Surely in the future, the developers of this app will take it easy on customers during an inflation of literally everything.

reviews.title: Great in theory
reviews.contents: This app is great in a lot of ways but has some big things that drive me crazy. First of all, I paid a lot of money for this set of apps and get there is no way to turn off the subtle adds and the way it tries to push you into ridiculous groups that might have nothing to do with you or babies. Just stop!! Also, maybe I just don't know how to work this app but I want a simple daily summary at the end of the day about at least the basics that is easy to locate and use. There's now a weekly summary which is a big improvement, but I still have to count ounces  myself to see how many my baby ate today. I don't think the weekly average insight things are enough. I also wish there was a little more customization and that I could hide things I can't use yet like (teething or breastfeeding) and then unhide them again later. Lastly, I am a foster parent of a newborn and that is part of why I wish there was a little more flexibility in choosing what you need. In this day and age there are so many different kinds of families and people raising babies that it would make sense to me to be more sensitive to these things when creating the app. It's clearly aimed at bio mothers (which I get is obviously the majority), but other people need these features too. Over all this app has some great features and we have used it for our daughters first three months of life, but I wish they would get rid of unnecessary clutter or at least give the option to customize and turn things off!

reviews.title: Great app to track baby’s daily habits!
reviews.contents:
I am a first time mom who is breastfeeding so a tracking app is 100% necessary to keep my brain straight! I love how I can keep track of everything from my daughter’s diaper change, including it’s color and consistency, to her feedings whether they are just on the breast or a mixture of breast, bottle, formula etc. I also love that my husband or whichever caregiver I allow access can add their own logs of diapers, feedings, activity, or whatever happens when they are taking care of her. My daughter is having slow weight gain so being able to pull the data into a CSV to share with my doctor is also super helpful. 

The one thing I would love to see is notifications. Being able to set notifications like when the next feeding is approaching or if we haven’t logged a diaper in a few hours would be EXTREMELY helpful. We have a thousand things going on as new parents and sometimes have to go play catch-up on logging items is a little inconvenient. Smart notifications that we can set through the app would be very helpful. 

Another wishful item would be a Home Screen widget to quickly add the diapers or start the breastfeed or sleep timer. Would save a click or two which could be super helpful 😃

reviews.title: Tracking with a lot of clutter
reviews.contents:
I enjoyed this app at first. I even bought the premium subscription while I was still pregnant. Tracking works well, and when the watch app works properly, it’s handy. BUT... they keep adding silly features that get in the way. The “AR” photo book seems gimmicky and I wouldn’t trust it to work reliably. They are always sending notifications about silly posts in the forums... Now the stories! So much clutter and nonsense! It’s too bad because I like the tracking features and use them pretty religiously. 

I’ve been trying some other more streamlined trackers, and currently like Huckleberry because we’re in the throes of sorting out nap time and it helps guesstimate when the next nap should be. (And it’s not such a train wreck when I open it up!)

Apple Watch app... ugh. Bit of a let down. First: It’s easy to accidentally lose the reading. In the phone app you can leave the timer and it keeps running, but on the watch, if you hit back it cancels it. So many lost sleep tracks! Worse: it displays the times differently than the phone and makes me do math to estimate when the last nap ended! For some reason they tell you when the last one started and how long it was - but not in minutes, in hours! E.g. 1:25pm, 1.4 hours long. So it ended.... errr... how many minutes is .4 hours? 20 something? This is not kind to users who are not sleeping well!!

reviews.title: App keeps getting unnecessary “upgrades” that ruined it
reviews.contents:
Dear Glow Baby developers,

What is wrong with you? Why do you keep “upgrading” / changing the app and making it less and less caregiver friendly? I used to be able to set the start and end time for my infant’s last/night sleep from the time I put her down to her anticipated waking time in the morning based on her average for her age or my past experiences. When she actually woke up, I’d edit the waking time from the anticipated time logged. Then, you went ahead and “improved” the app and made it impossible for me to project a waking time past 11:59pm of the current day. Now, you’ve gone ahead and “improved” the app to prevent me from projecting ANY future waking time. I don’t have the time, energy, or phone battery life to spare to have a timer running in the background until my child wakes up the next morning! I paid the full lifetime price for this app when my baby was born and you guys are actively robbing me of the conveniences I paid for. WHY???  

I initially gave this app 5 stars and even wrote and posted a long and detailed review. Having done so, it was EXTREMELY annoying getting constant reminders and requests to rate and review this app over and over again even after I had done so twice, once via my phone and once via my iPad.  Now I’m just livid that in addition to the aforementioned annoyance, you keep removing convenient features and adding useless ones. I WANT WHAT I PAID FOR! My original version of Glow Baby.

reviews.title: GREAT for tracking, Terrible articles (never get the premium!)
reviews.contents:
I LOVE all of the tracking features of Glow. I’ve been tracking my nine month old’s feedings, sleep, diapers, and my pumping sessions since the day he was born. It’s been incredibly helpful and so so so critical to caring for him everyday. I make sure he gets enough sleep, that his feedings are on track, and monitor his waketimes so I can get him down for his next nap on time. 

However, don’t EVER pay for the premium!! We did and it was terrible. As in, the articles are AWFUL. Which is funny because I typically agree with the information in the articles, so it’s not that I feel differently than the info they’re providing. It’s that the articles feel thoughtless, come across as judgemental and are VERY poorly written. They rarely answer a question thoroughly, they usually just tell you all the things you’re doing wrong as a mom (so not helpful), and sometimes they’re only two sentences long! And we PAID MONEY for them! It’s seriously crazy how unbelievably BAD they are. It’s like they’re trying to do the least amount of work possible. 

I ended up getting in touch with them and sent them a bunch of the articles that I felt were good examples of the poor quality. They simply said they would “look into it” and I didn’t hear anything more. Needless to say, I wasn’t happy with that answer, so we ended up getting our money back, which wasn’t easy through the App Store. Just stick with the tracking and don’t even bother looking at the articles. They’re really just that bad.
